examples.japanese: スープを{温|あたた}める。
{寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}は、お{風呂|ふろ}にゆっくり{入|はい}って{体|からだ}を{温|あたた}めるのが{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: On cold days, the best thing to do is take a long bath and warm up your body.

notes:
{温|あたた}める means to warm or heat something, particularly food, drinks, or body parts.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {温|あたた}まる (intransitive) - to become warm

KANJI DISTINCTION:
- {温|あたた}める: to warm objects, food, body ({温|おん} = temperature)
- {暖|あたた}める: to warm rooms, air, atmosphere ({暖|だん} = warmth)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- スープを{温|あたた}める: to heat up soup
- {体|からだ}を{温|あたた}める: to warm one's body
- {手|て}を{温|あたた}める: to warm one's hands
- お{弁当|べんとう}を{温|あたた}める: to heat up a lunch box

CONVENIENCE STORE PHRASE:
{温|あたた}めますか？ 'Shall I heat this up?' - commonly asked when buying food at a コンビニ.
